subject: arts-music
essential_question: How can understanding design, media, and material exploration help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Create, test, or revise a meaningful product that applies mixed media and the unit standards.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of mixed media.
Check, revise, or improve work about mixed media using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about mixed media.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 9 of "Design, Media, and Material Exploration" (unit 2, grade 8) is a performance-task increment on mixed media. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Solve a communication or environment design problem through multiple prototypes. Today's work contributes to that by handling mixed media at the performance task build stage, against the unit's wider topics of graphic design foundations, photography concepts without requiring people, mixed media, and three-dimensional or spatial design. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Advance your unit performance piece by one reviewable increment, drawing on mixed media. Before you begin, write where the work stands and what finishing today's increment would concretely look like. Make only that increment, then check it against what you wrote. Update a working log with the date, what you changed, what you tried that did not work, and what you kept. Name the next increment and the part you are most worried about. No audience, recording, or photograph is required — the log and the work itself are the evidence. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about mixed media, and it belongs to "Design, Media, and Material Exploration", which also covers separate topics such as graphic design foundations. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about mixed media; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 8 the bar is independent work that anticipates the obvious objection: name the case most likely to break your result, test it, and report what happened.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task about mixed media., The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
Address the lesson objective: Create, test, or revise a meaningful product that applies mixed media and the unit standards.
Produce the deliverable for a performance-task increment: One completed increment, the updated working log, and a named next increment with its main worry.
Show the process, not only the result — a working log, draft, or annotated study.
Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: One completed increment, the updated working log, and a named next increment with its main worry.
critique_criteria: The starting state and a concrete definition of the day's increment were written first.
One increment was completed and checked against that definition.
The working log records date, what changed, what was tried and abandoned, and what was kept.
The next increment and the most worrying part are both named.
No audience, recording, or photograph was required as evidence.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This work spans sessions, so supply a written milestone plan, explicit checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown. Executive-function load — sequencing, holding the plan in mind, remembering where the work stopped — must not become a silent part of what is being assessed.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting mixed media.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for mixed media follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for mixed media, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for mixed media works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of mixed media, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking mixed media mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply mixed media under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on mixed media rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
